data.name: Settings.Hardware.Switch
data.value: Read temperatures, fan speeds and power draw

data.name: Settings.Hardware.Help
data.value: Adds the temperatures, fan speeds and power draw of the processor, graphics card, mainboard and drives as metrics. Home Assistant creates no entity for them until you enable it there.

data.name: Settings.Hardware.Warning
data.value: The sensors of the processor and the mainboard can only be read through the kernel driver PawnIO. You install it yourself, separately from QoffeeAutomat; the agent never installs a driver. A kernel driver runs with the highest rights that Windows has, so install it only from its official source and keep it up to date. Antivirus software may warn about hardware monitoring drivers. While this switch is off, neither the hardware library nor the driver is loaded. Switching it off closes the connection to the driver at once; the library itself leaves memory at the next restart of the agent.

data.name: Settings.Updates.Switch
data.value: Check for a new release once a day

data.name: Settings.Updates.Help
data.value: The agent asks the GitHub releases page of the project for the newest version once a day and tells Home Assistant, which then offers the update. This is the only request the agent makes to the internet on its own; it sends no identifier of this PC. With the switch off no request is made and Home Assistant cannot tell whether an update exists.

data.name: Settings.Hardware.State.driver_missing
data.value: Running without the driver: the kernel driver PawnIO is not installed, so only the sensors that need no driver (drives, most graphics cards) are read. Install PawnIO to add processor and mainboard sensors.
